credit_line: Photo: National Park Service, Shenandoah National Park
what_it_shows: Black-and-white NPS photo of Ranger Roy C. Sullivan in uniform with a 'ROY SULLIVAN' name tag and NPS badge, holding his straw flat (campaign) hat. The crown of the hat has a burned-through hole from a lightning strike. The EXIF date of 2007-03-21 is the scan date; the photo itself is from the 1970s.
best_segments: Still. Hero/hook image. Suggested moves: slow push from full figure to his face (top ~45% of frame), then a second push onto the burned hole in the hat (lower-right quadrant, about x 0.45-0.95, y 0.50-0.80).

credit_line: Lightning footage: Stefan von Halenbach (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)
what_it_shows: Real night-time cloud-to-ground lightning, several separate strikes hitting behind a silhouetted line of conifers and trees, Germany, 2008. The source is 1 fps, so there are 19 distinct real frames; the mp4 holds each frame for 1 s at 30 fps. Cut it as a strobe, about 4-8 frames per still, rather than letting it play in real time. It is not Shenandoah and not one of Sullivan's strikes. Use it as the generic 'bolt' visual.
best_segments: full-sky white flash, bolt hits the ground at the centre, treeline silhouette (most violent frame)
single forked bolt to the ground behind the trees, then a bright channel
thick violet bolt striking the ground just left of the conifers
branching bolt crawling across the sky into the treeline
notes: Contact sheet lightning_germany_slowmo_pd.mp4-contact.jpg starts at t=2.0 s (each tile is 0.5 s).

license_evidence: Commons LicenseShortName 'Public domain'; category PD-self (own work by Stefan von Halenbach, 2008); was a Commons 'Media of the day'.

what_it_shows: The same storm in real time (25 fps, with sound). A multi-stroke cloud-to-ground flash flickers for about 0.5 s over the treeline and is pitch dark otherwise. Good for a real-speed strobe hit or a flash-frame transition.
best_segments: dark, then a multi-stroke bolt flickers over the tree silhouettes from 7.32 to 7.84 s, peak frames at 7.40, 7.48 and 7.56 s
notes: Square-pixel rescale of the 720x576 (SAR 59:54) original. Audio is kept as AAC (ambient and thunder).

archival: handshakes with CCC enrollees
